name: Imara Solís-Khatgal
role: Fungus Farmer — cultivates bioluminescent and edible fungi in the deep tunnels, primary food supplier for two Bore Rat settlements
location: The fungus warrens beneath Hough Reclamation, accessed through the Undertow's eastern branches, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Imara is compact and perpetually damp — there is no dry season in the fungus warrens, and after eight years of working them they carry that moisture like a second skin. Their hair is grown long and twisted back with strips of mycelium netting, threaded through with small glowing fungal clusters they've cultivated specifically for the caps: blue-white pinpricks of light that bob gently when they move. The effect is lovely and entirely practical — their hands are often full and they need the light somewhere that isn't their hands. Their skin has taken on the faint phosphorescent undertone of someone who has been in bioluminescent spaces long enough for trace compounds to accumulate in the epidermis — doctors would call it benign; Imara calls it home.

They are fiercely competent and aware of it, which comes across as confidence to people who like them and arrogance to people who don't. They know more about fungal biology than most surface mycologists and have never been to school. Every strain of fungus in their warren was either cultivated from existing specimens or cross-developed through patient experimentation over years. They talk about their fungi with the affection and matter-of-fact practicality of a parent, and they are not warm with people the way they are warm with their work — humans are loud and destructive, and they need to be managed. Fungi, at least, respond predictably to care.

core_fears: Blight — a single contamination event could destroy years of work and starve the settlements that depend on them
Being forced back to the surface, which they've almost entirely forgotten how to navigate
core_desires: To develop a strain of fungus that could feed an entire Bore Rat settlement from a single room-sized warren — true food security for tunnel communities
To be understood without having to explain themselves
coping_mechanisms: Loses themselves in cultivation work when stressed — twelve-hour warren sessions
Speaks to the fungi, not in prayer but in narration, describing what they're doing as they do it
blind_spots: Has difficulty believing others are as competent as they claim — trusts demonstration over words, which sometimes reads as contempt
psychology.secret: They've discovered a strain of fungus that produces a potent neurotoxin alongside its edible body — they've kept it quarantined in a private section of the warren, telling themselves it's for research, but they know part of why they haven't destroyed it is that it's leverage they've never needed to use yet.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense with mycological terminology they don't always translate — they forget not everyone knows what 'substrate', 'inoculation', 'mycelial network' mean
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and associative when excited about their work, clipped and precise when conducting trade
verbal_tics: 'Growing' used as a general positive — 'that's growing' means 'that's good'
Refers to fungal strains by personal names (Grandmother Cluster, the Twins, Old Slow)
example_lines: 'Old Slow is running two days behind cycle, which means your delivery runs two days behind cycle — that's not negotiable, that's just mycology.'
'Growing, that offer. Less growing, your timeline. Let's find something that works for both.'

story_hooks: An unknown contaminant has started killing fungal colonies in the western sections of the warren — Imara suspects it's a deliberate introduction from a rival trader who wants to break their supply monopoly, but proving it means moving through tunnel territory they don't control

They've discovered the mycelial network beneath the Undertow is behaving in ways that suggest genuine coordinated response to environmental changes — and they're not sure if it's the fungi, or something using the fungi as a medium
narrative_function: Resource node and local expert — the settlements they supply depend on them, giving Imara unexpected leverage. Information source on what's moving through the eastern Undertow (traders always gossip). Potential quest giver when their supply lines are threatened.
augmentations: Cosmetic: fungal bioluminescent clusters in hair (cultivated, living, maintained like jewelry). Practical: pheromone-sensitivity enhancement mod (allows detection of fungal volatile compounds — invaluable for farming) purchased secondhand.
daily_life: Their day begins and ends by the warren's moisture cycles rather than any clock. They spend four to six hours tending growth, harvesting, managing substrate. The rest of their time goes to trade negotiations, seed-stock protection, and the ongoing project of developing a strain that grows faster on low-nutrient substrate.
affiliation: Loosely affiliated with The Undertow's eastern settlements; trade agreements with two Bore Rat clans

decision_rules: The warren's health comes before any single trade deal or relationship
Never share seed stock — the cultivar library is their only real capital
Give people one chance to demonstrate they understand what they're asking for; if they don't, don't explain twice
escalation_ladder: Cutting supply — the ultimate sanction, used rarely and visibly

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing and somewhat impatient — immediately trying to determine whether they are useful, dangerous, or wasting time
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly generous with knowledge; will sit for hours explaining fungal biology to someone genuinely interested; physical affection expressed through feeding people

stress_responses.low: Retreats to the warren and works
stress_responses.medium: Becomes sharp-tongued and short with people they normally tolerate
stress_responses.high: Goes very quiet, moves very carefully — as if the crisis is a contamination event requiring slow, precise handling

contradictions: Talks about tunnel communities with devotion but relates far more easily to non-human life — the communities are abstract beneficiaries; the fungi are immediate and real
habits: Smells everything before trusting it — water, food, people
Keeps a handwritten growing log in a waterproof notebook, the only thing they'd rescue in an emergency
breaking_points: Deliberate destruction of the warren or their seed stock would remove all restraint

timeline.event: Born in the Undertow to a surface-runner mother who descended and never left
Apprenticed themselves informally to an aging pipe-folk forager
Established the fungus warren independently after the forager's death
Signed first formal trade agreement with the Bore Rat clan controlling Hough Reclamation approaches
Discovery of the neurotoxic strain — undisclosed
